item.title: Wheat Extends July Rally as War Risks Stoke Fears Over Supply
item.description: Wheat resumed its rally after a brief bout of profit-taking, as escalating geopolitical tensions and worsening weather in key producing regions continued to stoke supply concerns.

item.title: Malaysia Sells First Dollar Bonds in Five Years as Fuel Subsidy Bill Rises
item.description: Malaysia raised $1.5 billion in its first dollar bond sale in five years, bolstering funding as the Southeast Asian nation grapples with a fuel subsidy bill that’s likely to more than double from an initial goal due to the Iran war.

item.title: India’s SEBI Mulls Letting Portfolio Managers Invest Clients’ Money Overseas
item.description: SEBI proposes allowing investment in overseas securities and IPO-bound firms, among others.

item.title: Manipal Health Seeks to Raise Up to $960 Million in India IPO
item.description: Manipal Health Enterprises Ltd. is seeking to raise as much as 92.7 billion rupees ($960 million) in an initial public offering, continuing a run of sizable share sales in India.

item.title: Asian Allies Push Back Against Trump’s Forced-Labor Tariffs
item.description: Asian nations have described the Trump administration’s latest tariffs as baseless and unjustified, while stopping short of any retaliatory moves.

item.title: China’s Gold Imports Surge After International Prices Slump
item.description: Chinese gold imports rose to a two-year high in June, underscoring resilient demand in the world’s biggest bullion market after a plunge in international prices.

item.title: Chinese Stock Turnover Shrinks as Sentiment Cools on Tech Sector
item.description: Chinese daily stock turnover dropped to the lowest level in over three months, as investors shun the nation’s technology sector.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama Says to Take Bold FX Steps Decisively as Needed
item.description: Japanese authorities will take bold steps to counter moves in the currency market decisively as needed, and a US Treasury report issued overnight underscores a shared view that excessive currency moves are undesirable, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said.

item.title: Trump to Take Up Manila’s Concerns With Xi, Philippines Says
item.description: US President Donald Trump assured Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that he would take up Manila’s concerns when he meets with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Southeast Asian nation said.

item.title: SK Hynix, Samsung and Kioxia Face Pivotal Earnings Test on AI Swings
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. are set to test investor appetite for memory chips as South Korea’s stock market — now a bellwether for global AI sentiment — grapples with violent swings driven by leveraged chip bets.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippine Peso Falls to Fresh Record Low as Oil Advances
item.description: The Philippine peso fell to a fresh record low as oil prices climbed, boosting pressure on the central bank to intervene as markets eye 62 as the next key level.

item.title: Macquarie’s First Woman CEO Departs With a $339 Million Stake
item.description: Shemara Wikramanayake is stepping down as head of Macquarie Group Ltd. after leading the Australian financial conglomerate to bumper profits and a record high share price. For that she will be richly rewarded, making her one of the best-paid female bank executives in the world.

item.title: Modi Seeks to Calm Anger in Rare Video as India Protests Widen
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a fresh bid to calm mounting anger over examination paper leaks as students prepared nationwide protests on Friday, with demands growing for the education minister to step down.

item.title: Here’s the Full List of Trump’s New Tariffs on 60 Economies
item.description: The US will collect duties of between 10% and 12.5% on imports from most major trading partners, its biggest move yet to reconstruct President Donald Trump’s tariff wall that was pierced by the Supreme Court. The following is a list of tariffs announced on July 23, according to the US Trade Representative.

item.title: PBOC Adds Most Liquidity to Economy in Five Months to Aid Growth
item.description: China’s central bank made its biggest addition of liquidity to the economy in five months via its medium-term lending facility to support growth ahead of its late July Politburo meeting and to accommodate government bond issuance.

item.title: Yen’s Worst Week Since May Brings It Close to 165 Versus Dollar
item.description: The yen is on track for its biggest weekly loss in more than two months, with intervention warnings doing little to deter investors betting on further weakness.

item.title: Singapore Pushes Back as US Levies Hit on Forced-Labor Claim
item.description: Singapore’s top diplomat said there was no economic justification for the US to impose tariffs on the city-state, adding that it seeks to avoid becoming “collateral damage” in Washington’s broader trade policy.

item.title: Top Environmental Fund Sees Japan Key to AI Energy Challenge
item.description: Asia’s best-performing environmental fund has increased exposure to Japan as it expects the nation’s technology sector to prove increasingly pivotal in solving the artificial intelligence industry’s surging power demands.

item.title: S. Korea Moves Up Leveraged ETF Deposit Rule to Tame Volatility
item.description: South Korea is moving up the date it had planned to lift the minimum cash deposit requirement for investors in leveraged exchange-traded funds to July 31, a measure to curb demand for the products that are blamed for amplifying stock volatility.

item.title: CXMT’s Frenzy Ignites Hopes of Futher Hardware Rally in China
item.description: Investors are looking to Monday’s trading debut of CXMT Corp. to help renew a rally in Chinese semiconductor stocks that has been on pause ahead of the memory giant’s initial public offering.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline as Surging Energy Costs Raise Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold held a retreat as the widening conflict in the Middle East pressured energy prices and increased expectations the US Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy to contain inflation.

item.title: Japan’s Inflation Picks Up, Keeping BOJ on Path for Rate Hikes
item.description: Japan’s key inflation gauge picked up for the first time in three months, keeping the Bank of Japan on course for another interest-rate hike this year.

item.title: UK Consumer Confidence Recovers to Pre-War Levels, GfK Says
item.description: Britons put the Iran war energy shock behind them this month as the soccer World Cup and Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s promise to help with living costs lifted the national mood, according to a survey.

item.title: Singapore MAS Set to Hold on Mild Inflation, Signal Tightening
item.description: Singapore’s subdued inflation will likely allow the central bank to maintain its monetary policy settings on Monday, while it assesses the potential impact of a resurgence in the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: Japan Is Whipsawing Wall Street’s CLO Machine, Study Shows
item.description: The $1.3 trillion US CLO market is taking its cues from Tokyo as much as Wall Street.

item.title: Robotics Startup Genesis in Talks to Raise About $500 Million
item.description: AI robotics startup Genesis AI is in talks with investors to raise around $500 million in a new funding round, according to people familiar with the efforts.

item.title: Trive-Backed Lyntris Files For US IPO, Joining Defense Rush
item.description: Lyntris Inc., a defense technology firm backed by Trive Capital, filed for a US initial public offering.

item.title: Historic Yen Slide Poses New Risk to Japan Stocks’ Bull Run
item.description: The yen’s relentless slide is raising concern that it risks eventually curbing the foreign inflows that have helped propel Japanese equities to record highs.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Fall as Oil Surges Past $100: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were poised for declines after a sharp Wall Street selloff, while oil surged above $100 a barrel for the first time in two months as an escalating Middle East conflict stoked fears of renewed inflation.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 24
item.description: Oil headed for a weekly surge after Houthi attacks on tankers in the Red Sea opened a new front in the Middle East conflict, while President Donald Trump threatened to extend US strikes on Iran.
